title: Capacity stress scenarios by region - 2026 Q4 rollout plan
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet captures a compact sensitivity matrix for GPU capacity across NA / EU / APAC, plus an operable rollout timeline for Q3–Q4 2026. Intended audience: infra on-call, platform schedulers, SRE, and product ops. This is an iterative draft focusing on stress windows and automated warm pools, not the canonical regional forecast doc.

Key constraints & assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model mix: 60% 30B-class (higher mem), 25% 7B-class, 15% embeddings/encoders.
- Baseline target P95 latency budget: 350ms for hosted API text-generation in NA; EU and APAC budgets are 400ms/450ms respectively.
- Baseline utilization target: 65% average steady-state; bursting allowed to 90% for <12h windows with reserved spill to Dedicated.
- Typical instance types (cloud-agnostic names): GPU-A100-80GB (heavy), GPU-A40-48GB (medium), GPU-T4-16GB (light).
- Cold-start KV-cache miss penalty: +20% token cost and +40–80ms latency depending on model class.

Scenario matrix (3 baseline stress scenarios):
1) Ramp (organic growth): +35% sustained traffic over 90 days.
   - Actions: add 12% permanent capacity in NA, 8% in EU, 10% in APAC; enable additional autoscale headroom (+15%) over 30d.
   - Impact: P95 latency drift +10–15ms if no migration; cost +18% qtr-over-qtr.
2) Flash-viral (spike): 3x peak for 6h in a single region.
   - Actions: immediate cross-region spill (route 25% to nearest region), warm-up scheduled warm pool to 65% in 15m, fall back to smaller quantized variants for 30% of requests.
   - Impact: if no warm pool, expected P95 > 1s and error rate increases.
3) Cloud-zone outage (zonal loss): 40% of regional capacity down for 48h.
   - Actions: prioritized failover of critical customers to Dedicated; preempt non-critical batch jobs; enable multi-zone routing policy and standby Dedicated nodes.
   - Impact: scheduled SLO exceptions and throttling for non-critical tiers.

Sensitivity table (text representation):
- Metric axes: traffic delta (x-axis: -10%, 0%, +25%, +50%, +100%), capacity buffer (y-axis: 5%, 15%, 30%, 50%).
- Quick read: NA needs buffer >=15% for +25% traffic; EU needs >=30% buffer for +50% traffic; APAC needs >=30% for +50% traffic due to fewer local spare zones.

Regional capacity snapshot (planned additions H2 2026):
- North America:
  - Planned add: 320 A100-80 GPUs (equiv) distributed across 3 cloud zones.
  - Warm-pool target: 55 nodes (A100-equivalent) with KV-cache prewarm for top-20 customer prompts.
  - Expected utilization after add: from 68% -> 62% steady.
- Europe:
  - Planned add: 140 A100-80 GPUs (equiv) with supplementary 220 A40 equivalents for medium workloads.
  - Warm-pool: 25 A100-equivalent prewarmed nodes, prioritized for enterprise rollouts.
  - Expected utilization after add: 72% -> 65% steady.
- APAC:
  - Planned add: 180 A100-80 GPUs (equiv) but distributed in 2 major regions with smaller zone sizes; include 80 A40-equivalents to smooth variance.
  - Warm-pool: 30 A100-equivalent, higher warm-up latency allowance (targets relaxed by 10%).
  - Expected utilization after add: 70% -> 63% steady.

Rollout timeline (milestone-driven, sprint alignment):
- Week 1–2 (Mar 2026): finalize procurement SKU mapping and cross-cloud node equivalence table; freeze model-variant set for warm pools.
- Week 3–4 (Apr 2026): deploy warm-pool orchestration in NA staging; run 3 simulated spike tests (3x6h).
- Week 5–8 (May 2026): deploy to EU with adjusted warm-pool sizes; integrate billing-metering hooks for prewarmed nodes.
- Week 9–12 (Jun 2026): APAC phased deployment; validate KV cache replication and region sticky routing.
- Week 13–18 (Jul–Aug 2026): cross-region failover rehearsals, SRE runbooks dry-run, finalize canary thresholds.
- Week 19–24 (Sep–Oct 2026): put full fleet into production with staggered capacity ramp (20% weekly increments), monitor cost and latency impact.

Operational controls and runbook notes (short):
- Autoscale settings: aggressive-horizontal up to 30% within 10m for NA; conservative for EU/APAC (20% within 15m) due to zone sizes.
- Warm-pool policy: TTL 6h with rolling refresh every 4h if top request patterns persist.
- Fallback policy: auto-quantize 30% sample when P95 > 750ms for >5m.
- Cost throttle: activate per-customer soft rate limit when cost-per-token delta > +25% vs baseline.

Risk items and open questions (to resolve before final sign-off):
- Exact procurement lead time for A100-equivalent reserved instances in primary NA cloud; current vendor quote variance ±21 days.
- Bandwidth and KV-replication RPO for APAC—needs engineering spike to validate 95th percentile prewarm times.
- Impact of model-architecture changes (attention kernel changes) on kernel selection heuristics in runtime causing non-linear performance shifts—request SRE+runtime benchmark in next 2 weeks.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: coordinate SKU mapping and update pricing model (due 2026-03-08).
- Marcus: run NA staging 3x6h spike test and upload results (due 2026-03-20).
- Olga: implement warm-pool TTL control in orchestration (PR link above) and add observability metrics (due 2026-03-15).
- Diego: validate APAC KV replication RPO and report (due 2026-03-18).

Appendix: quick cost note (rough):
- Incremental monthly cloud bill for planned adds ~ $1.6M (NA 820k, EU 380k, APAC 400k) assuming reserved discounts; expected to increase hosted revenue capture by reducing tail latency and enabling more enterprise customers.

Status note: this is a working sheet intended for iterative updates; next revision after NA staging tests are completed.
